about: Your vault: the reading account (and other features' data) carried between devices in an encrypted vault, after newsroom.sgit.ai's Vault pane (a beta there). Read by newsroom/build/features/account.mjs into the pane's config. Nothing here is secret: the endpoint is the public vault server newsroom.sgit.ai uses, and the access key itself is never written to this repository.
library: sg-vault v0.2.3 (assets/vendor/sg-vault/v0.2.3, unedited) and its one local extension (assets/vendor/sg-vault/local/sg-vault--create-with-id.js)
door_constant_why: The passkey's PRF input and the door's derivation salt name this site, so an account made here is this site's own and never opens, or is opened by, a newsroom.sgit.ai account.

access_key.what: A vault access key: the token the vault server asks for before it accepts a write (sent as the x-sgraph-access-token header to the endpoint above and nowhere else). Opening and reading a vault needs none; creating one, and updating it, does.
access_key.where: Not issued yet. Dinis Cruz will add how readers of this site get one; until then the pane asks for it, explains what it is, and creates nothing without it. Once pasted, it is written into the reader's own master vault, so no other device of theirs needs it typed.
access_key.never: The key is never written to this repository, never kept in local storage, and never sent anywhere but the endpoint above.

recovery.shown: Your recovery code, shown once. Print it or save it now:
recovery.why: Without this code and your passkey, nobody can open this vault, not even us. It opens a second door to the same vault, for a device without your passkey and for the day the passkey is gone. This page does not keep it.
recovery.ask: To go on, type the last four characters of the code
recovery.wrong: That does not match the end of the code. Check what you wrote down.
recovery.done: Recovery code confirmed. It is not kept anywhere on this page.

onboarding.hint: The pilot gives every reader a key from a public pool, so no one has to ask for one. Your browser makes your own keys first, which takes a few seconds.
onboarding.ready: A pilot access key is ready: now create your vault.
onboarding.empty: The pool is empty for now. Try again in an hour, or tell us you are interested.
onboarding.failed: No pilot key could be drawn:
onboarding.claimed: Your vault was made and your claim was posted.
onboarding.claim_failed: Your vault was made. The claim could not be posted, which does not affect your vault.

mail.duplicate: Another reader drew the same pilot key first, so a new one was given to you. Your vault is not affected.
mail.rekey: Your pilot key was replaced. Your vault is not affected.
mail.refused: A message could not be checked and was ignored.

doorcode.button: No passkey? Use a door code
doorcode.title: A door code instead of a passkey
doorcode.hint: Without a passkey your door is made from a code of 26 characters that you keep, as you would keep a password. Anyone with the code can open your vault, and without it nobody can, not even us.
doorcode.bad: That is not a 26-character door code.
doorcode.novault: No vault answers to this code.
doorcode.shown: Your door code, shown once. Save it in your password manager or download it now:
doorcode.ask: To go on, type the last four characters of the code
doorcode.wrong: That does not match the end of the code. Check what you saved.
doorcode.file: This file holds the key to your PrompTugal.news vault. Anyone who has it can open the vault. Keep it as you keep a password, and delete it once it is in your password manager.
